subject: feat(auth): implement AuthSessionCache for OAuth2 child sessions (#985)
body:
Cache contextual and table-scoped OAuth2 child sessions so that context
credentials do not trigger a token request on every catalog call (#962).

AuthSessionCache:
- Expire entries after auth.session-timeout-ms without access (default
  1 hour), and when the token of an OAuth2 session expires.
- Load each key once under concurrent Get() calls, with the loader
  running outside the lock. Failed loads are not cached.
- Hand every removed session to the removal listener exactly once. A
  session loaded after Close() is removed immediately.
- Sweep expired entries periodically on the auth refresh executor, every
  session timeout clamped to [1s, 60s]. Without an executor, entries are
  reclaimed when accessed again or on Close().

OAuth2Manager:
- Cache contextual sessions by session_id and table sessions by token.
- Authenticate child token requests with the parent session's headers.
- Credential child sessions follow token-refresh-enabled and, with
  refresh enabled, require the auth executor. Token and exchange child
  sessions do not refresh until refresh via token exchange is supported.
- Token child sessions no longer carry the parent's credential.

OAuth2Session:
- Add StopRefreshing(), a non-blocking stop used on cache removal.
- Add ExpiresAt() and IsRefreshable(), and include the session headers
  in OAuth2Info().

subject: feat(parquet): add statistics-based row group filtering (#956)
body:
## What

Adds `ParquetMetricsRowGroupFilter` to evaluate Iceberg predicates against Parquet footer statistics before reading row groups.

Adds tests covering split intersection, non-contiguous row groups, physical row positions, unprojected filter columns, schema evolution, missing statistics, predicate binding, and delete handling.

## Why

The Parquet reader previously selected row groups only by file split. Filter predicates could not eliminate row groups whose footer statistics ruled out matching rows.

## Behavior change

- Enables statistics-based pruning by default through `read.parquet.row-group-filter.enabled`.
- Retained row groups still require residual predicate evaluation; this does not implement exact row filtering.
- Physical row positions and row IDs remain correct across pruned row groups, even when a batch spans multiple row groups.
- Negated range predicates preserve boolean NOT semantics for nulls. Predicate negation adds a null check, and out-of-range comparisons retain null checks when folded.

subject: feat: apply write defaults in DataWriter (#942)
body:
Writing a batch with an older schema should fill omitted columns with Iceberg
write-default values. This PR adds optional `DataWriterOptions::input_schema`;
for a required column with initial-default 42 and write-default 7, input
`[[1], [2]]` writes `[[1, 7], [2, 7]]`.

DataWriter prepares a reusable `WriteProjection` once in `Make` and applies it
to each batch. The projection matches fields by ID recursively, preserves
supplied values and explicit nulls, fills missing optional fields with typed
nulls, and materializes missing fields from their write-default. When no
`input_schema` is provided, or the schemas are identical, the original Arrow
batch is passed through without projection.

Incompatible schemas fail before opening the file, including extra input IDs,
missing required fields without a write-default, optional-to-required fields,
and concrete-to-unknown writes. Existing primitive types must match; read
projection behavior is unchanged.

Parquet and Avro writers remain unchanged and continue to expect batches
matching their complete target schema. The shared projection is implemented in
core using nanoarrow shared buffers without adding an Arrow C++ dependency.

Addresses the write-path portion of #637.

subject: fix(build): pin croaring, nlohmann_json, spdlog, cpr, sqlpp23 fetches (#1082)
body:
These FetchContent downloads had no integrity pin, unlike Arrow,
nanoarrow, and utf8proc in the same file, so a tampered archive or
mirror would be compiled unverified. nlohmann_json keeps a URL_HASH
(its tarball is a stable uploaded release asset). The other four use
GitHub's auto-generated tag-archive endpoint, which is not byte-stable
across requests and cannot be hash-pinned reliably (confirmed: the
same tag download returned different checksums on different
requests), so they switch to GIT_REPOSITORY + GIT_TAG pinned to the
tag's full commit SHA, the same pattern already used here for Avro,
googletest, and google_benchmark.
